claims.claim: The work is the account of the trial and death of Maximus, a merchant from Asia who was martyred under the emperor Decius.
The occasion was Decius's edicts, which ordered all Christians to sacrifice to the gods and renounce their religion.
Maximus declared himself a Christian openly, was arrested, and was brought before the proconsul Optimus.
The text is a question-and-answer interrogation between the proconsul and Maximus, in which Maximus refuses to sacrifice to the gods.
Maximus was beaten with cudgels and stretched on the rack, and he would not recant.
Optimus condemned Maximus to be stoned, and he was led outside the city and stoned to death.
Wikipedia says the evidence for the story is an acta that belongs to the 'proconsular acts', a text made by the clerk of the tribunal.
Alban Butler's Lives of the Saints presents his account as drawn from the original acts in Surius, Baronius, Henschenius, Ruinart, Fleury, Tillemont and others.
The Roman Catholic feast of Maximus is April 30.
